subject: Customer Q: Data residency, retention and deletion for Private/VPC deployment
messages:
From: Luc Schmidt <luc.schmidt@eu-retail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anika Muller <anika.muller@eu-retail.com>
Date: 2026-02-11T07:43:00Z
Subject: Data residency and deletion guarantees for Private/VPC deployment

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the Private/VPC option looks promising. Before we progress to a POC, our security and legal teams need written confirmation on a few points about data residency, retention and deletion:

1) In a Redwood Private (VPC) deployment, can you confirm that customer application data (prompts, responses, model artifacts, logs) can be stored in our own cloud account and remain within the EU?
2) What is the exact deletion workflow if we request full purge of a dataset (including backups and snapshots)? Timeline and proof of deletion would be helpful.
3) Do you support customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK) / HSM for encryption-at-rest and key rotation?
4) How are snapshots/backups handled — do they replicate cross-region by default? If so, can replication be disabled?
5) What audit/evidence can Redwood provide after deletion (deletion certificate, audit logs)? What is the expected SLA to complete deletion requests?

Our compliance team also asked for a short SOC2 summary and a diagram of data flows for the Private/VPC installation. Can you share these and indicate any limitations (e.g., control plane vs data plane architecture)?

Appreciate a concise Q&A we can attach to our internal review.

Thanks,
Luc
Security Architect
EU Retail GmbH

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Luc Schmidt <luc.schmidt@eu-retail.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-12T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Data residency and deletion guarantees for Private/VPC deployment — Q&A

Hi Luc / team,

Thanks — below is a concise Q&A tailored to a Private/VPC deployment. I’ve focused on the items you flagged. If you want formal contract language (data processing addendum) we can draft that after the call.

Q1: Can customer data be stored in the customer account and remain in the EU?
A1: Yes. For Private/VPC we deploy the data plane into customer-controlled resources. In cloud deployments we provision or attach to customer-owned object storage (S3-compatible) or block volumes in the customer’s cloud account and region (e.g., eu-west-1). Data does not leave the region unless you explicitly enable cross-region replication or choose a control-plane-hosted backup option.

Q2: Deletion workflow (full purge including backups/snapshots) — timeline and proof
A2: Deletion process (standard flow):
- Step 1: Customer submits deletion request via support portal or signed DPA addendum. We acknowledge within 72 hours.
- Step 2: Mark data for deletion in the application and remove pointers from live stores (immediate).
- Step 3: Initiate purge of object storage / block volumes in customer account via customer-managed IAM role (if cloud) or operator runbook (on-prem). Purge includes: primary objects, model cache, and KV caches.
- Step 4: Delete snapshots/backups according to the snapshot provider API. If backups are in the customer account we call the provider API to remove snapshots (typical completion window: 24–72 hours depending on provider).
- Step 5: Cryptographic shredding (if BYOK) — if you use customer-managed KMS keys we can rotate and then revoke access as an additional mitigation; we can provide key-revocation logs.
- Step 6: Final verification & certificate of deletion — we provide a signed certificate detailing the objects removed, replication status, and timestamps. Standard completion target: 30 days from acknowledgement, except where legal hold or regulatory requirements prohibit purge.

Notes:
- If you host backups in your account, Redwood will perform API-driven snapshots/deletes using the permissions you grant; we do not independently move backups outside your account.
- For on-prem installs, deletion is executed per customer runbook; we provide the deletion steps and an auditor-friendly checklist.

Q3: Customer-managed KMS / HSM (BYOK)
A3: Supported. We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Google CMEK, Azure Key Vault) and support BYOK patterns. Key usage is scoped to your account and we do not retain plaintext keys. For HSM workflows, we support customer-provided HSM-backed keys; integration requires a short setup window to configure key policies and access delegation.

Q4: Snapshots/backups replication defaults & control
A4: By default we do not enforce cross-region replication for Private/VPC deployments. Replication is only enabled if you explicitly configure it (or select a multi-region DR option). You can disable replication in the deployment manifest or via our infra automation before provisioning.

Q5: Audit/evidence after deletion
A5: We provide:
- Deletion certificate (signed PDF) listing objects removed, approximate sizes, and timestamps.
- Audit logs of the deletion orchestration (who initiated, when, API calls made) streamed to your logging endpoint (e.g., CloudWatch/Stackdriver or your SIEM) if you configure our logging sink.
- If requested, we can provide tamper-evident hashes of deleted object manifests prior to deletion for external auditors.

Additional operational notes:
- KV cache: ephemeral caches used by the runtime are in-memory with optional local disk; we evict and purge caches as part of the deletion workflow.
- Control plane vs data plane: For Private deployments you can choose a private control plane (hosted in your tenancy) or a Redwood-hosted control plane. If you choose Redwood-hosted control plane, metadata (deployment state, billing pointers) may be stored outside your VPC, but all customer content can remain in your tenancy. We can provide a minimal metadata footprint option if required.
- Retention configuration: Retention windows (soft-delete, hard-delete timelines) are configurable per-tenant. Default snapshot retention is 30 days; we can extend or shorten per contract.

Open caveat: If a legal hold or preservation order is in effect, deletion will be paused and we will notify you immediately; we will provide export/eDiscovery support instead.

Attachments: deletion-playbook.pdf (playbook + auditor checklist)

Happy to jump on a call to walk this through. If you want specific contract language for DPA and Data Residency clauses I can draft a redline.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai

From: Luc Schmidt <luc.schmidt@eu-retail.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anika Muller <anika.muller@eu-retail.com>
Date: 2026-02-12T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Data residency and deletion guarantees for Private/VPC deployment — follow-up on legal hold / eDiscovery

Thanks Maya — very helpful. A couple of follow-ups:

1) We have regulatory requirements to retain certain audit logs for 7 years, but we also need the ability to purge PII on request. Can you support both (i.e., long-term retention of anonymized logs + per-PII deletion)?
2) For the deletion certificate: will it include a list of object identifiers (e.g., S3 keys) or just a summary? Our auditors prefer object-level detail where possible.

Also, can you confirm the SLA around deletion completion if no legal hold exists (you mentioned 30 days target)? Is there a faster option for emergency purge?

—Luc

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Luc Schmidt <luc.schmidt@eu-retail.com>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-12T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Data residency and deletion guarantees for Private/VPC deployment — next steps

Hi Luc — quick answers and proposed next steps:

- On the long-term retention vs PII purge: yes, we can support retention of anonymized/aggregated audit logs while purging customer-identifiable data. That is typically implemented by a two-tier retention policy and an anonymization pass before an archive operation.
- Deletion certificates: we can provide object-level identifiers (S3 keys, snapshot ids) where we have API access to the storage provider. Where the storage is fully in your control and you prefer not to share object keys, we can provide a signed summary plus hashes.
- SLA: Standard target is 30 days from acknowledgement for full purge (no legal hold). Emergency purges are possible — we offer an expedited remediation path (target 72 hours) subject to operational approvals and depending on the cloud provider’s snapshot semantics. Expedited purges are covered under enterprise SLAs / addendum.

Next steps:
1) I’ll set up a 30-minute call with your security team and our infra/security leads to run through the deletion playbook and draft DPA language.
2) I’ll send the SOC2 summary and deletion-playbook.pdf (attached) and a short checklist for your auditors.

Suggested call times (CEST): Thu 2026-02-13 09:00–11:00 or Fri 2026-02-14 14:00–16:00. Which works for you?

Thanks — talk soon.
